steps.content:
May 23, N.F. 115
City-State Security Bureau (Newly Established)

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: Six months have passed since the assassination of the Speaker and the cabinet overthrow. The 9th Agency has just completed its third round of citywide screening for Outland spies. Our investigations have covered 2,038 people, resulting in 198 suspects identified and 117 arrests.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: They're all bribed DisCity locals, mostly recruited through the dark web. They know nothing about their employers and only care about pocket change. In other words, the real mastermind stays well hidden.

Lotherlon
Guillotin's successor, Interim Chief of the Outland Affairs Bureau, recently appointed to Max King's Cabinet.

steps.speaker: Lotherlon
steps.content: All Outland ambassadors have been summoned for questioning in connection to suspicious activities during the election. We've also widened the investigation to include all organizations tied to the Outland. Notably, Quinn's president has been detained for allegedly bribing councilors. The full reports have been forwarded to the 9th Agency.

steps.speaker: Lotherlon
steps.content: The borders are now under stricter lockdown, with heightened scrutiny for all entries and exits. So far, no individual or organization has claimed responsibility for the attack.

Lang
Chief of the newly established Eastside Defense Bureau, member of Max King's Cabinet.

steps.speaker: Lang
steps.content: Tch, you expect criminals to willingly confess? Of course they're the ones who killed those people. The Outlanders couldn't wait to reap the benefits from it!

steps.speaker: Lang
steps.content: With a prize like the new mine, Nirvana has been haggling with the Syndicans for over a year, only to stay empty-handed. The Outlands would be fools not to act. Letting DisCity monopolize it is not an option. What's there to fear? War is simply another form of negotiation!

steps.speaker: Lang
steps.content: The FAC has long since shifted its focus to Mania defense. The Black Rings and Corruptors have drained the military budget dry, our soldiers and artillery tied up defending the Broken Frontline. A single Tide of Ashes or a DisSea surge, and they're already stretched thin. If war actually breaks out, how many troops would we even have left?

steps.speaker: Lang
steps.content: Anyone with a brain can see this is the Outlands' best—if not last—chance to cripple DisCity. And yet, here we are, entertaining fantasies of the "Great Expo," rolling out the welcome mat for thousands of them?

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: Because this is a peace petition actively proposed by our ally Fraser. An outright refusal would damage DisCity's standing—we can use that as the official position to present.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: What I care about is that, as the only <color=#fb9259>friendly city-state</color> that stood by our side during the last Outland war, Fraser has promised crucial intelligence. Not just about the cabinet attack's true perpetrators, but about the world beyond our walls.
The communicator before the empty seat across the table crackles to life. You know that voice. Your former boss, the Silver Spider. Her tone regarding the Great Expo seems deliberately noncommittal.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: The good old days... The last expo was in N.F. 106. What should have been a peaceful celebration ended with a diplomatic collapse, and we still haven't truly reconciled to this day.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: The widespread disasters have limited war, trade, and transportation, but they've also choked off intelligence networks. For every ten agents we send out, we're lucky to get back a single corpse with half a dying message. That's another kind of isolation.
Through the communicator, you hear her fingernails lightly tapping on the table. It's her habitual gesture when deep in thought.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: We hear blades being sharpened, yet we're still blind in this fog. DisCity needs real intelligence. We must see every threat before it strikes. And if a blade is pressed to our throat? We take it... and follow it straight back to its master.
[Small CG - Jelena's Trio in Fire]
The screen flickers to life, displaying the final image of Sinner Jelena, the Outland spy. The room falls silent as everyone watches, then all eyes turn to you.

steps.speaker: Langley
steps.content: Please, Chief ${PlayerName}, we need first-hand intelligence from the MBCC.
You rise to your feet, gazing at that footage you have watched countless times, and begin stating your "findings" in a perfectly flat tone.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Sinner Jelena was previously detained by the MBCC, and we had conducted a comprehensive examination of her physiology and Mania status. The results confirmed her as an A-Class Sinner back then, though with underdeveloped powers that hadn't yet manifested into any clearly defined external expressions.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This was inconsistent with the incident where the Underground Puppets were controlled and enhanced to attack the former cabinet. As a result, we initially ruled out Jelena as a suspect, concluding she lacked combat capabilities and wasn't operational personnel.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Then...
[Small CG - War image only, no Jelena, 1s] (But no one witnessed this scene, not sure if we should show it here.)
[Small CG - Parting with El at the Hospital]
Your gaze sweeps the meeting room. The Silver Spider remains silent, showing no sign of any input.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: No complete report was ever compiled for this attack. Even my own memories of the event have been fragmented and unreliable. When we conducted another comprehensive examination on Jelena, her Mania showed fluctuations but remained within A-Class parameters. Just as before, she showed no signs of developing stable, externally manifested combat capabilities.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: Nevertheless, we proceeded with extreme caution, increasing surveillance while working to verify our suspicions. What we ultimately discovered about her... surpassed even our wildest imagination.
[Small CG - Before Boss Battle]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: During this full-scale operation, Jelena didn't employ her own power. Instead, she was channeling something else, a force far more powerful.
[Weapon Portrait]

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: This is an Ash Crystal. During that battle, we witnessed the Outland spy resonating with it, unleashing Mania power remarkably similar to that of Calamity Apostles.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: It's not something an A-Class Sinner can withstand. I believe she must have employed some form of powerful external medium.
At your gesture, a stream of light flows from Schorl beside you. It takes control of the screen signal, further enlarging the image and automatically enhancing the pixelated footage.
[Zoom in on weapon: Aurum Secretum] (Maybe we can use PV here?)

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: The Ring Research Institute has verified Chief ${PlayerName}'s speculation.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: During the final battle, the decorative metal on the Outland spy's hand activated an unusual resonance trait. It minimized the Mania differential between this Sinner and the Ash Crystal, granting her temporary synchronization with an Apostle of Ashes and access to its immense power.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: However, this metal is not a natural substance but an artificial, extremely precise cutting-edge creation—technology that DisCity has yet to comprehend.

steps.speaker: Lang
steps.content: ...This doesn't look good. This thing clearly isn't some amateur creation. It must have required massive resources and manpower to develop. Whoever's backing her is no small player.

steps.speaker: Lang
steps.content: Hey, where's that spy now?

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: She made a desperate final stand, then vanished. Due to Jelena's excessive use of the Apostle's power, her resonance with the Ash Crystal completely altered her original Mania traits.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: The shackles have broken. I can no longer track her.

steps.speaker: Lotherlon
steps.content: On the bright side, our enemy hasn't fully mastered this power yet, and that Sinner is already dead. On the more concerning side... we've only exposed one spy, one who infiltrated DisCity years ago. For all we know, our enemy may have already created more soldiers like her.

steps.speaker: Lotherlon
steps.content: You're right. Intelligence is crucial. We need more intel from the Outlands.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: Gathering local intel takes time. While we successfully dismantled the Underground's dark web last August, the operation came at a steep price. Many of our agents in the Outlands were exposed, went missing, or were neutralized, with classified materials leaked in the process.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: Our intelligence network has been severely compromised. Both rebuilding and reactivating it will take considerable time. If we can't afford such a long wait—

steps.speaker: FAC Commander
steps.content: Then let Fraser bring their "intelligence" to us. If they dare attempt anything underhanded, we'll be fully prepared to prevent any incidents.
An FAC officer stands up, salutes the group, and proceeds to take charge of the report.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander
steps.content: First, we'll segregate all Outland delegations entering under the Great Expo banner. Only a select group of high-ranking officials will be permitted inside city embassies as diplomatic envoys, while the rest will be housed in the "Outland quarters" outside the city.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander
steps.content: These "quarters" will be under FAC's close surveillance, ensuring that the majority of their personnel, goods, and information are strictly confined to the designated area outside our borders.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander
steps.content: Second, we'll implement targeted countermeasures against the Apostles of Ashes. Now that our enemy has revealed their attack methods, we'll adapt our defenses accordingly. Every lesson learned from fighting the Tide of Ashes will be put to good use.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander
steps.content: Third, we'll coordinate with satellite towns and other allied forces to reinforce outskirts patrol routes and alert systems. This will prevent any large-scale force from approaching the city undetected.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander
steps.content: Simulations confirm that even if the enemy were to mobilize from the nearest city-state, traversing the calamity-stricken WhiteSands would exhaust their time and resources. Should conflicts erupt during the Great Expo, our existing defensive capabilities are more than adequate to protect our city.
He stands firm, distributing more detailed strategies to each leader in attendance, sparking a serious discussion around the conference table.

steps.speaker: Lotherlon
steps.content: We should accelerate our Expo preparations, then. Can't afford to let them notice anything unusual and gain diplomatic leverage against us.

steps.speaker: Lang
steps.content: Naturally. History's greatest warmongers always draped themselves in peace banners first—the better to lull their enemies into complacency. Time to see who can stand till the end in this game.

steps.speaker: 9th
steps.content: Since Fraser has managed to persuade several minor factions to share intelligence and mend relations, we should capitalize on this opportunity to sort out friends from foes and gain a clearer assessment of the situation.

steps.speaker: FAC Commander
steps.content: Looking on the bright side, if nobody causes trouble and the Great Expo proceeds smoothly, this could be exactly what the Hypercube economy needs. Nirvana has been particularly enthusiastic about this prospect.

You notice that the 9th Agency has cut off the communication at some point, and the FAC Commander-in-Chief, who should have been present, is nowhere to be seen. Throughout the entire meeting, he hasn't even called in.
Besides that, there is another absence that catches your attention... You scan the "new cabinet" members gathered around the table, yet their supposed leader is nowhere to be found.

steps.speaker: Option
options: Will Speaker King approve of this?

steps.content: In response to your question, a member of Max King's Cabinet catches it and almost reflexively rolls his eyes.

steps.speaker: Lang
steps.content: The Speaker? Huh, he won't oppose anything. What can he actually accomplish anyway?

steps.speaker: Before you can finish your question, McQueen hops on the MBCC vehicle that's come to your rescue, pulling you on with her. The vehicle revs and speeds away, leaving the fuming building in the dust.

steps.content: The call ends, but Schorl continues to hover in mid-air beside you, showing no intention of leaving.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: When Jelena was first captured, you appeared quite dejected, but now you're able to view the situation objectively.

options: It's what I'm supposed to do.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: Your growth in intelligence work is truly remarkable. That being said...

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: MBCC has taken custody of that girl and refused to hand her over to the Stewart family. Have you obtained any information from her?
You glance at Schorl, finding only your own eyes mirrored on its surface. The emotions behind your gaze remain hidden.

options: No leads. The kid doesn't know anything.
Right, I'm also waiting for her to talk.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: But I should have the right to take her in. Given her connection to Sinner Jelena, she doesn't really have anyone trustworthy left outside.
Schorl falls momentarily silent, eventually conceding to your decision.

steps.speaker: ${PlayerName}
steps.content: I'll notify you if there's any update?
Schorl's approval of you has increased.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: After all, she's a highly emotional Sinner with straightforward reasons for joining this conflict. Such individuals are particularly impressionable, and dangerously effective at inciting others. Emotional vulnerability breeds susceptibility to manipulation.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: However, Chief, if you had experienced it yourself, you would understand that war operates on an entirely different scale from personal feelings. It's not a stage for individual emotions. One cannot survive such conflicts on sentiment alone.

steps.speaker: Schorl
steps.content: The enemy is constantly seeking to overthrow DisCity and upend the existing world order. This is the harsh reality we face, one we must meet with absolute clarity.
[Show Jelena's Flashback]
